name: Timișoara Traian Vuia International Airport
before:
Romania's fourth busiest airport and the main hub for the west of the country and the Danube-Criș-Mureș-Tisa Euroregion, serving Timișoara in the Banat region.

Its runway is one of only four in Romania longer than 3 km, alongside the two Bucharest airports and Constanța. That capability, plus its position, means it acts as a backup airport for Belgrade, Bucharest and Budapest when those close.

It is an operating base for Wizz Air.

There are two passenger terminals. Terminal A, built in 1964 and modernised in 2002, doubled in size at the end of 2010 and was dedicated to non-Schengen destinations and domestic flights, handling 500 passengers an hour across three gates. Terminal B, from 1980 and modernised in 2004, is the larger, handling 800 passengers an hour across nine gates. Romania's Schengen position has changed since those designations were set, so confirm which building a client needs.

The airport is named after Traian Vuia, the Romanian flight pioneer, who was from Timiș County.
after:
Romania's fourth busiest airport and the main airport for the west of the country, 12 km north east of central Timișoara. It handled nearly 1.46 million passengers in 2025.

Its 3,500 m runway is one of only four in Romania longer than 3 km, alongside the two Bucharest airports and Constanța.

Wizz Air flies from here to more than 20 destinations, most of them in Italy and Germany, as well as to London Luton.

A new arrivals terminal for international flights opened in July 2021, followed by a departures terminal for Schengen flights in March 2024. The airport's departures board now puts the London Luton flights at Terminal 1, while most other flights use Terminal 2.

It is named after Traian Vuia, the Romanian flight pioneer.

claims.claim: Romania's fourth busiest airport (2025)
claims.note: Eurostat 2025, all Romanian airports that report: Bucharest Otopeni 17.0 million, Cluj 3.55 million, Iași 2.24 million, Timișoara 1.46 million, then Suceava 0.77 million. Brașov and Constanța do not report to Eurostat; the Romanian Airports Association's 2025 chart (a picture on its 3 February 2026 release, so not quotable here) gives them 337,353 and 119,426 and shows the same top four, with Timișoara on 1,458,098. Eurostat's dataset was last updated on 17 September 2026.

claims.claim: the airport's departures board: London Luton at Terminal 1, most other flights at Terminal 2
claims.inAfter: The airport's departures board now puts the London Luton flights at Terminal 1, while most other flights use Terminal 2.
claims.note: Attributed to the operator and checked against its own live board, 23 September 2026. That board, read on 23 September 2026, lists 44 departures over the next three days: the 9 at Terminal 1 all go outside the Schengen area (London Luton, Istanbul, Antalya, Monastir, Hurghada, Larnaca), and the 35 at Terminal 2 go to Schengen countries or Bucharest. No second, independent source for the terminal split was found (Wizz Air's site answered 405), so the text states only what the airport's board shows and does not name the old Terminal A and B.

claims.inAfter: It is named after Traian Vuia, the Romanian flight pioneer.
claims.note: The operator's history brochure (a 2015 article it republishes) dates the name to 2002; Wikipedia gives 6 February 2003. The year is not in the text.
